## R for Geospatial Analysis

While our primary focus is QGIS, R is another powerful tool for spatial data analysis and visualization. Below are curated external resources to help you learn R for geospatial work.

### Recommended Courses

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Rbanism Geospatial Data Carpentry
A comprehensive introduction to working with geospatial data in R, focused on urban applications.

**Topics covered:**
- Introduction to R and RStudio
- Working with vector data (sf package)
- Working with raster data (terra package)
- Spatial operations and analysis
- Creating maps with ggplot2

[Visit Course →](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/r-geospatial-urban/)
:::

### Community Challenges

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## #30DayMapChallenge
Join the annual mapping challenge! Create 30 maps in 30 days using R and share with the community.

**What you'll learn:**
- Daily mapping practice
- Data visualization techniques
- Creative problem-solving
- Community engagement

[Learn More →](https://30daymapchallenge.com/)

[Rbanism Challenge Resources →](https://github.com/Rbanism/30DayMapChallenge)
:::

### Additional Resources

#### Books & Documentation
- [Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/) - Comprehensive guide to spatial analysis
- [Spatial Data Science](https://r-spatial.org/book/) - Advanced spatial data methods
- [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) - General R programming foundation

#### Key R Packages
- **sf**: Simple features for vector data
- **terra**: Spatial data analysis for raster data
- **tmap**: Thematic map creation
- **leaflet**: Interactive web maps
- **ggplot2**: Data visualization

### Why Learn Both QGIS and R?

QGIS and R complement each other well:

| QGIS | R |
|------|---|
| Visual, interactive interface | Code-based, reproducible |
| Quick exploration | Automated workflows |
| Print-ready maps | Statistical analysis |
| Beginner-friendly | Powerful scripting |

**Pro tip:** Use QGIS for exploration and map design, then use R for reproducible analysis and batch processing.
